learning: Executed facts from the real trace: (a) the C128 decode step is uniformly memory-bandwidth-bound at 74.2% of the 273 GB/s theoretical peak - attention 225-232 GB/s (82.6-85.1%), per-layer GEMM 199 GB/s (73.0%), lm_head 214 GB/s (78.5%); the three independent class estimates agree within 15%, which is what falsifies a launch/latency-bound reading (the 545 MB lm_head GEMM reaches the same per-byte efficiency as the 40-260 us per-layer GEMMs). (b) The 5.0% non-attention/non-GEMM surface (softcap 6.25 ms, argmax 5.00 ms, RMSNorm 3.90 ms, act 3.52 ms over 16 forwards) bounds any fusion/skip idea to <1% of the step; softcap is mathematically argmax-preserving for greedy, but its whole value is ~1.1% of decode time on ~half the weighted score (~0.5%), below gate noise, so it is not proposed. (c) Per-layer attention durations are flat (585-608 us) and the sliding/full group difference is -1.1%, opposite to the <=3.1% window-binding prediction at seq 513-528: a NULL control at decode length, not evidence about the 8192-token prefill path. (d) Config-derived byte accounting explains the measured step: 2.88 GB non-embedding weights + 0.545 GB lm_head + 3.76-3.88 GB KV per forward at 202.6 GB/s = 35.5 ms, matching the measured 35.46 ms. (e) New discrepancy: the same efficiencies predict 6302-6974 tok/s at DC-C256 versus the branch-recorded a1 reference 5162 tok/s (18-26% gap); the supplied trace cannot decide whether this is anchor comparability or a real bs=256 cost.
